label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: Legged desks with lower shelves, a standing chalkboard, ceiling fans, floor, walls and ceiling are recognizable beyond generic cubes.

The repeated desks face the front, but their uniformly spaced grid loses the reference's denser, uneven arrangement. Identical narrow wall panels do not reproduce the varied doors and bright openings.
Desks appear too low and small relative to the tall openings and room; backpacks reach approximately desktop height. The front stage assembly occupies too little of the end wall.

The broad color categories are present, but pale tan furniture replaces dark brown wood, yellow walls are subdued, and nearly uniform illumination loses the strong side-opening daylight and shaded front recess.

Box.123 is a finite nonempty mesh with 8 vertices, 6 polygons and dimensions 1.55 × 0.64 × 0.10, bound to SceneActSurface_6. Ball has 482 vertices, 512 polygons and depth on all axes. Bound materials contain Principled BSDF connections to Material Output.

The authored view clearly evokes the supplied classroom through repeated wooden desks, yellow lower walls, overhead fans and a green board before a burgundy and green stage surround, despite substantial simplification.

dimension_scores.evidence: The classroom and distinctive front color arrangement are recognizable, while openings, furniture density and architectural detail diverge.
Desktops have visible supporting legs and fans have downrods. Most objects appear grounded, though the board stand lacks a convincing stabilizing base and wall shutters read as attached slabs.
Yellow, cream, green, burgundy and blue cues survive, but furniture is excessively pale and bags and curtains have rigid block silhouettes.
Consistent shading gives spatial depth, but slab curtains, blank pictures, box-shaped bags and uniformly repeated furniture make the room look like a rough model.
Forward-facing rows, central circulation and side-wall features preserve basic organization. Excessive regularity and generous spacing weaken the reference arrangement.
Furniture is undersized relative to openings and enclosure, bags are large relative to desks, and the stage surround is comparatively narrow.
Soft contact shadows are coherent, but broadly flat illumination and similar uniform surfaces lose the reference's side lighting and distinction between wood, floor and fabric.
Numerous desks, fans, bags, books and the front board are included. Visible chairs, ceiling beams and tube lights, detailed doors and stage-side furnishings are absent or unrepresented.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
